coverage.evidence: Supply-chain pinning is the heart of this change. zizmor found four unpinned action references in this project's own pr-checks.yml, all now pinned to the commit behind their v5 tag, and two checkouts persisting the job credential in .git/config, both now persist-credentials: false. zizmor went from 13 findings with 6 high to a pass. Every tool the new workflow runs is pinned by binary checksum, image digest or rules commit.

The input boundary in scope is the filename the regex reads, and its worst case was exercised deliberately at 1,001 / 5,001 / 20,001 / 50,001 / 100,001 characters, each built to match then fail at the final character. That is the abuse case for the rule Semgrep raised, and it was run rather than reasoned about.

summary: Pass, light depth. The change strengthens security rather than touching an attack surface: four unpinned actions pinned to commits, two persisted job credentials dropped, a mutable gitleaks action replaced by a checksum-verified binary, and dependency scanning introduced where there was none. The one code hunk is a comment and a rule-specific suppression, with the claim behind it measured.
